history.summary: A genuinely large 1561sqft freehold 3BR in D14 (Paya Lebar) at a very low $1089 psf — roughly 11% below the project's $1222 URA median, a meaningful discount for a freehold near Aljunied MRT. The headline 6.6% resale CAGR rests on only 6 transactions so it is statistically unreliable, but the absolute value and freehold tenure are real.
history.rating_rationale: $1.7M for a 1561sqft freehold 3BR in a Paya Lebar Central district works out to $1089 psf vs $1222 median — about an 11% PSF discount. Freehold + sub-$1.8M (liquid band) + D14 airbase-relocation/PLC catalyst. The oversize means a buyer is getting land-banked freehold space cheaply; even if the 6-txn appreciation rate is noise, the entry PSF gives margin of safety. Built 2007 (19yr, dated but not problematic).
red_flags: Appreciation rate from only 6 transactions — unreliable, treat as illiquid resale market
Large 1561sqft pushes quantum but tenant rent won't scale with size (yield drag on a 3BR resale)
19-year-old development — maintenance/refurb costs, less modern facilities
catalysts: Freehold tenure at $1089 psf — well below district new-launch PSF
Paya Lebar Central commercial hub and Paya Lebar airbase relocation unlocking land long-term
Discount to project median PSF gives entry margin

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: D14/Aljunied has a deep tenant pool (city-fringe, MRT-served). A 1561sqft 3BR rents to families but yield is modest given the quantum; rent does not scale with the oversized floor area.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 6-txn resale rate is unreliable; lean on tenure + entry discount rather than the 6.6% figure. Freehold D14 at this PSF should track RCR ~5%, with downside cushioned by the below-median entry.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Discounted from 6.6% (only 6 txns) to a conservative freehold-RCR estimate

history.summary: Genuinely below the going 3BR rate ($1,089 vs ~$1,307 PSF), but the discount is largely size-driven (a big 1561 sqft unit) on a 19-year-old, 28-unit Geylang freehold with very thin transaction depth, so the 'value' is soft and liquidity is the binding constraint.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,089 PSF (1561 sqft, $1.7M). Verified 3BR pricing at The Midas averages ~$1,307 PSF (listings $1,193-$1,446; a 1141 sqft 3BR recently at $1,446 PSF), so $1,089 is real-cheap on PSF — but a 1561 sqft unit is at the large end and large units structurally trade at lower PSF, so the v3.4 cohort comparison overstates the bargain. Critically, the appreciation is a regional_baseline fallback on just 6 txns and psf_cohort_txns=1, so the -34.6% age-adj and -6% cohort figures rest on near-zero comparables (data quirk territory). Built 2007 (old_property flag) and only 28 units = very thin, illiquid market with wide bid-ask. Freehold and D14 location are pluses but neither is a forward edge. A patient own-stay-style buyer could find real space value here; as a 5-7yr investment the illiquidity and absent catalyst cap it at Neutral with low confidence.
red_flags: Cheapness partly an artifact of large 1561 sqft unit vs pooled 3BR PSF; size-adjusted discount is smaller
Appreciation is a regional_baseline fallback on only 6 txns; psf_cohort_txns=1 (single comparable)
Tiny 28-unit, 2007-built project = very low liquidity and wide spreads
Geylang sub-locale can drag financing/resale demand
catalysts: Freehold tenure on a large 3BR floor plate (space value for own-stay/long hold)
Walkable to Aljunied MRT in an established D14 estate
